name: 2025.05.07 Item 6C - Planning Commission Meeting Material Received
agenda_text:
May 5, 2025

Larry Springs, Chairman
Carolyn Fowler, Commissioner District 1
David Rice, Commissioner District 2
Aidé Trejo, Commissioner District 3
Cheryl Shaw-Williams, Commissioner District 4

RE: Opposition to Proposed Rezoning and Development of Beach Avenue/La Colina
Drive

Dear Commissioners,

I am writing to respectfully urge you to vote no on the proposed rezoning and development
application affecting 20 parcels within the Downtown Inglewood and Fairview Heights
Transit-Oriented Development (TOD) Plan area—including my own home, which I have
owned for 32 years. My property lies directly east and south of the proposed site and is
included in the proposed rezoning.

I bring both personal and professional perspectives to this issue. I have spent my career in
community development, including 20 years as Executive Director of Inglewood
Neighborhood Housing Services and, most recently, as CEO of Chattanooga Neighborhood
Enterprise. Throughout my career, I’ve focused on creating strong, inclusive neighborhoods
through affordable and mixed-income housing. In December 2024, our work in
Chattanooga was honored with the Jack Kemp Excellence in Affordable and Workforce
Housing Award from the Urban Land Institute. The award recognized our leadership in
integrating middle-density housing into urban areas in a way that respects existing
neighborhood character. You can review our body of work—highlighting what appropriate
urban inﬁll development should look like—here:
https://www.cneinc.org/_ﬁles/ugd/036083_af5cc3bf33644f2e9d46f3235b084e6b.pdf

Our work in Chattanooga demonstrates how denser development can be thoughtfully
implemented on these 20 parcels, respecting the character of the existing community
while also providing the much-needed housing our region requires.

As both a longtime resident and an expert in the ﬁeld, I have deep concerns about this
rezoning proposal—particularly regarding the La Colina parcels. While I support increased
density on the Don Lee Farms site due to its proximity to a commercial corridor, the
expansion of this rezoning to include La Colina is inappropriate, unjustiﬁed and just plain
BAD PLANNING.

This marks the third attempt to signiﬁcantly upzone property on La Colina. Each time, the
neighborhood has voiced strong opposition—particularly due to La Colina’s unique
topography and strained infrastructure. In 2019, Councilman Padilla directed that these
 concerns be addressed. Instead of doing so, the current proposal disregards both
community feedback and guidance from elected officials, opting instead to further
increase the scale and potential negative impacts.

There are numerous issues with this proposal. Below are some of my speciﬁc objections
and concerns:

1. Disregard for the TOD Planning Process
The rezoning application undermines the integrity of the 2016 TOD Plan, which was the
product of a 20-month community-led process involving technical analysis, public
workshops, and extensive stakeholder engagement. La Colina Drive and Beach Avenue
were both speciﬁcally studied, and their zoning designations were intentionally maintained
as R2 and M1. The TOD overlay already provides a 15% development bonus—additional
rezoning is not needed and was explicitly not recommended.

2. Lack of Transparency and Community Engagement
We are being told there is “no speciﬁc project,” yet there appears to be a conceptual plan
submitted by East Beach Inglewood LLC. Clearly, there is a development plan in motion,
but the developer is avoiding community scrutiny. If this rezoning is approved, any future
project could be built by-right, without additional review or community input. This is a clear
end-run around meaningful public process.

3. Inappropriate Zoning and Height Impact
While I understand and support the city’s need to meet its housing goals, forcing oversized
developments between established single-family homes at the request of a private
developer does not serve the neighborhood or the broader community. Responsible
development must be context-sensitive, planned with a clear understanding of what types
of housing and density are suitable for each area. Here, La Colina’s steep topography and
narrow, dead-end street make it particularly unsuited to high-density construction. These
physical constraints, along with the residential character of the block, should determine
what is appropriate to build.

The proposed MU-1 zoning allows a mix of commercial and high-density residential uses
that are incompatible with the existing neighborhood. It permits buildings up to nine stories
with no setbacks, and the EIR’s concept shows a ﬁve-story structure on the La Colina slope
that would loom 3.5 to 4 stories above surrounding homes, creating a stark visual and
physical impact.

Additionally, the EIR misrepresents the location of my home relative to the proposed
development. On page 3-15, my house is incorrectly shown to the east of the site, when it is
actually directly on the western property line. With MU-1 zoning requiring no side setbacks,
this could allow a building to be constructed just inches away. This misrepresentation
raises concerns about the accuracy and integrity of the review process and suggests other
information may also be inaccurately presented in favor of the proposal
 4. Traffic and Safety Concerns
La Colina is a narrow, dead-end street. When cars are parked along it, only a single
vehicle can pass. The EIR states that visitors will enteron La Colina Drive. However, the
study does not disclose or address the narrow conﬁnes of the street nor that there is
literally no parking anywhere close to the project as there is no parking on Florence Avenue
or Centinela Avenue. There may be a few spots on Beach Street which would be a block
away from the entrance. In addition, Beach Avenue is already congested with truck traffic
serving Don Lee Farms, with frequent backups that create blind spots and hazardous
conditions. Adding over 200 additional daily car trips to this already strained infrastructure
is irresponsible.

5. Violation of Planning Principles
This proposal abandons the thoughtful framework established in the 2016 plan by pushing
development to its maximum allowable intensity, without consideration for the surrounding
context. In contrast, even the nearby Don Lee Farms project is proposing a more measured
scale of three-story townhomes.

Zoning and community plans are designed to provide stability and predictability. Residents
make long-term decisions—where to live, invest, and raise families—based on these plans.
By moving forward with this rezoning, the City risks undermining not only the upcoming
comprehensive plan update but also the years of work and input from hundreds of
residents who shaped the original Transit-Oriented Development (TOD) Plan. What
message does it send when a developer with no ties to Inglewood can sidestep a
community-driven vision?

None of the La Colina property owners were consulted in the creation of this proposal.
When I raised concerns about my property being rezoned without my input, staff
responded by saying my home’s value would increase and that I could sell to a developer.
How is that an appropriate response to a legitimate concern about land use and
neighborhood stability? That’s not planning—it’s speculation. And it sends a troubling
message: if longtime residents don’t like the outcome, they should just leave. This feels
like a backdoor attempt to push out invested community members to make way for
outside developers and speculators.

In Closing:
I support thoughtful development that respects existing R2 zoning and takes advantage of
TOD and affordable housing bonuses to deliver much-needed housing. Best practices in
urban inﬁll call for adding density in a way that is context-sensitive—balancing the need for
more units with the character, scale, and fabric of existing neighborhoods. This proposal
disregards that balance.

You now face a choice: uphold a community-led vision shaped by years of local input, or
set a precedent that sidelines neighborhood voices in favor of outside interests.
 Thank you for your careful consideration.

Sincerely,

Martina Guilfoil

Cc: Bernard McCrumby, Jr
